children.name:
Own versioned portable channel-work history, confirmed uploads, immutable
      sealed snapshots and authorized continuation material independently of runtime
      or model-provider implementation types. Late evidence is archived separately
      from active execution authority.
terms:
"Own versioned portable channel-work history, confirmed uploads, immutable
      sealed snapshots and authorized continuation material independently of runtime
      or model-provider implementation types. Late evidence is archived separately
      from active execution authority."
"Store acknowledged typed records and verified content behind immutable hashed snapshots."
"A different runner must know exactly which work and workspace evidence is available."
"Do not import provider tokens, hidden runtime state, secrets or unrelated local conversations."

children.name: I35: Snapshots are immutable. A matching seal retry returns the original snapshot including sealedAt; a changed identity, content, requested cursor or hash fails HistoryConflict. canonicalHash is SHA-256 of versioned canonical ordered records, verified content hashes and provenance, never a client hash accepted without recomputation.
terms: "I35: Snapshots are immutable. A matching seal retry returns the original snapshot including sealedAt; a changed identity, content, requested cursor or hash fails HistoryConflict. canonicalHash is SHA-256 of versioned canonical ordered records, verified content hashes and provenance, never a client hash accepted without recomputation."

children.name: I35: Completeness covers only persisted and acknowledged sections and contents through throughCursor. Missing referenced content or gaps reject a Complete seal. Later sections and archived evidence do not alter an existing snapshot.
terms: "I35: Completeness covers only persisted and acknowledged sections and contents through throughCursor. Missing referenced content or gaps reject a Complete seal. Later sections and archived evidence do not alter an existing snapshot."

children.name: I36: Portable records contain only this channel-associated run, its human inputs with provenance, assistant messages, tool calls/results, attachments, prompt and compaction provenance, agent/instruction snapshots, turn/branch relationships, summaries and workspace artifacts. Reject secrets, unrelated conversations, opaque provider tokens and internal runtime state.
terms: "I36: Portable records contain only this channel-associated run, its human inputs with provenance, assistant messages, tool calls/results, attachments, prompt and compaction provenance, agent/instruction snapshots, turn/branch relationships, summaries and workspace artifacts. Reject secrets, unrelated conversations, opaque provider tokens and internal runtime state."

children.name: I37: Import and prepareContinuation confer no authority, execute no old tools, mutate no source run and never reuse the original runtime session. The caller starts a new linked run and attempt under freshly checked capabilities and current channel authority.
terms: "I37: Import and prepareContinuation confer no authority, execute no old tools, mutate no source run and never reuse the original runtime session. The caller starts a new linked run and attempt under freshly checked capabilities and current channel authority."

children.name: I38: Archive requires an active current runner key bound to the historical attempt, current channel access under participation or delegation, and a late-archive-only decision. An expired or superseded lease may archive evidence but may not append active history, mutate progress, authorize tools, seal an active result or publish a summary.
terms: "I38: Archive requires an active current runner key bound to the historical attempt, current channel access under participation or delegation, and a late-archive-only decision. An expired or superseded lease may archive evidence but may not append active history, mutate progress, authorize tools, seal an active result or publish a summary."

children.name: I39: Every continuation identifies sourceRunId, sourceAttemptId, snapshot.id, source summary and workspace evidence. Parallel continuations are independent; source records and snapshots remain unchanged.
terms: "I39: Every continuation identifies sourceRunId, sourceAttemptId, snapshot.id, source summary and workspace evidence. Parallel continuations are independent; source records and snapshots remain unchanged."

children.name: I40: prepareContinuation verifies every referenced repository, commit, diff and workspace artifact is resolvable and authorized. Missing working state, incomplete required history or missing effective skills/tools fails HistoryContinuationRejected. Native checkpoints are optional and accepted only on explicitly verified runtime/version/snapshot compatibility; requested incompatible or absent checkpoints are rejected.
terms: "I40: prepareContinuation verifies every referenced repository, commit, diff and workspace artifact is resolvable and authorized. Missing working state, incomplete required history or missing effective skills/tools fails HistoryContinuationRejected. Native checkpoints are optional and accepted only on explicitly verified runtime/version/snapshot compatibility; requested incompatible or absent checkpoints are rejected."

children.name: I47: Reject more than 100 records in one upload, more than 256 KiB UTF-8 canonical serialized section metadata and records, any content over 10 MiB, or more than 100 MiB distinct synchronized content per attempt. Measure actual bytes on the server, including late evidence. Never silently truncate.
terms: "I47: Reject more than 100 records in one upload, more than 256 KiB UTF-8 canonical serialized section metadata and records, any content over 10 MiB, or more than 100 MiB distinct synchronized content per attempt. Measure actual bytes on the server, including late evidence. Never silently truncate."

children.name: I11/I12/I14/I20: Human read authority derives from an opaque current Human Session credential, account standing and current channel access. Runner operations require the current runner key and either a valid bound channel delegation or durable participation. Authorize each referenced snapshot/content before return and recheck authority at persistence commit, rather than trusting supplied scope or IDs.
terms: "I11/I12/I14/I20: Human read authority derives from an opaque current Human Session credential, account standing and current channel access. Runner operations require the current runner key and either a valid bound channel delegation or durable participation. Authorize each referenced snapshot/content before return and recheck authority at persistence commit, rather than trusting supplied scope or IDs."

children.name: I25/I48: Section IDs and per-attempt sequences are immutable. Identical canonical retry returns the original acknowledgement and timestamps without second writes/events. Different content under the same section ID or sequence fails HistoryConflict. Only consecutive sections with a matching previousHash advance the confirmed cursor; a gap is rejected, never acknowledged as complete.
terms: "I25/I48: Section IDs and per-attempt sequences are immutable. Identical canonical retry returns the original acknowledgement and timestamps without second writes/events. Different content under the same section ID or sequence fails HistoryConflict. Only consecutive sections with a matching previousHash advance the confirmed cursor; a gap is rejected, never acknowledged as complete."

children.name: History append atomically stores its section, verified content batch and confirmed cursor. Any failure preserves all three complete collections. Canonical equality is structural and insensitive to JSON object field ordering; arrays retain order. Content IDs reused with a different hash or bytes fail HistoryConflict.
terms: "History append atomically stores its section, verified content batch and confirmed cursor. Any failure preserves all three complete collections. Canonical equality is structural and insensitive to JSON object field ordering; arrays retain order. Content IDs reused with a different hash or bytes fail HistoryConflict."

children.name: Append and seal require a current unsuperseded execution lease under server time. authorizeReader and authorizeContinuation require current channel read authority and recipient runner/snapshot capabilities, but never source-run lease ownership; these decisions grant no execution authority. A second runner can read and prepare a source snapshot without modifying its run.
terms: "Append and seal require a current unsuperseded execution lease under server time. authorizeReader and authorizeContinuation require current channel read authority and recipient runner/snapshot capabilities, but never source-run lease ownership; these decisions grant no execution authority. A second runner can read and prepare a source snapshot without modifying its run."

children.name: HistoryApi.humanSections constructs Human authority from its opaque session credential and run path, then uses the same authorizeReader and HistoryRepository.read contract as other history reads. Its cursor, limit, attempt, optional sealed snapshot and requested content references never bypass current channel authorization. Manifest remains metadata-only; section and content retrieval stays bounded and explicit.
terms: "HistoryApi.humanSections constructs Human authority from its opaque session credential and run path, then uses the same authorizeReader and HistoryRepository.read contract as other history reads. Its cursor, limit, attempt, optional sealed snapshot and requested content references never bypass current channel authorization. Manifest remains metadata-only; section and content retrieval stays bounded and explicit."

children.name: HistoryReadScope and HistoryAuthorizedScope are owner-issued decisions, not client identity proofs. The HTTP client never supplies them, and delegation credentials and Human Session secrets are never persisted in portable records or returned in manifests.
terms: "HistoryReadScope and HistoryAuthorizedScope are owner-issued decisions, not client identity proofs. The HTTP client never supplies them, and delegation credentials and Human Session secrets are never persisted in portable records or returned in manifests."
